# Observable removes the wrong same-named function listener

## Context

A non-blocking finding in [PR #20559's review](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/20559#pullrequestreview-5810734569) exposed a core listener-removal defect. The Store repair uses subscription IDs locally; the underlying function selector still removes the wrong closure. Grace independently captured the defect, and a direct current-source probe reproduced it.

## The Problem

Register two different functions from one factory, both named `handler`. Remove the second by function reference and fire the event:

```text
expected calls: ["first"]
actual calls:   ["second"]
sameName: true; sameFunction: false
```

`Observable.removeListener` accepts either reference identity or matching `.name` even when the caller supplies a Function. It scans in registration order, so the first same-named function is removed instead. An unregistered function can likewise remove a registered function with the same name.

## The Architectural Reality

Design authority: `src/core/Observable.mjs` documents removal by subscription ID, handler, or object-valued listener specification. `addListener` already distinguishes a Function reference from a String handler selector. The existing string-name path is intentional and remains supported.

The owning branch is `removeListener`'s object form; the direct Function overload delegates there. The same branch extracts `{fn, scope}` specs. `#13102` restored object-spec symmetry and `#14928` made parsing non-destructive; neither addressed name collisions. `#18236`'s declined change to structural function comparison is a different surface: this repair does not touch `Compare`, config equality or listener reconciliation.

## The Fix

Use reference identity when the removal selector is a Function. Permit function-name matching only when the selector is explicitly a String. Preserve scope matching, subscription IDs, first-match string behavior and non-destructive argument parsing.

Extend `test/playwright/unit/core/ObservableListenerObjects.spec.mjs` and retain `ObservableListenersDiff.spec.mjs` coverage. No new module or registry.

| Selector | Required matching | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Function, including object `{fn}` | The exact registered function in the requested scope; a same-named different function is not a match | factory-closure regression across all function forms |
| String in an object-valued spec | Existing named-handler semantics | string-name controls |
| Subscription ID / scope | Existing exact subscription and scope behavior | existing suites and new controls |

Decision Record impact: none; no change to function equality elsewhere.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: Red-first tests show direct, object-valued and `{fn}` removals remove the requested second closure, not the first same-named closure.
- [ ] AC-2: Removing an unregistered same-named function is a no-op.
- [ ] AC-3: Explicit String-name selectors, scoped listeners, subscription IDs, caller-owned input objects and config reconciliation retain their behavior.
- [ ] AC-4: The complete unit suite and CI pass; the fix does not replace or weaken #20559's subscription-ID cleanup.

## Out of Scope

`Compare.compareFunctions`, config-equality policy, changes to named String resolution, generic event architecture, and the Google Maps API migration.
